version: "2.11.6"

homepage: https://www.macports.org

    type: string
    default: /opt/local
    description: Installation prefix
  build_arch:
    type: string
    description: Target architecture for builds (e.g., x86_64, arm64). Usually auto-detected, clear after OS upgrade.
  universal_archs:
    type: string
    description: Architectures for universal builds (e.g., x86_64 arm64). Clear after OS upgrade.

  - ports

    "prepare": {
      "filename": "prepare.star",
      "content": "# macports/prepare.star - Prepare phase for MacPorts

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# The Xcode Command Line Tools are a fundamental dependency for MacPorts.
# Many ports require compilers and build tools provided by CLT.
# The Xcode license must be accepted after installation or updates.
# (Source: https://trac.macports.org/wiki/ProblemHotlist)

def prepare():
    """Check preconditions for MacPorts installation."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _prepare_darwin()
    return {"prepare": True}

def _prepare_darwin():
    """Check macOS preconditions for MacPorts."""
    # Check for Xcode Command Line Tools
    result = shell.exec("xcode-select -p", allowed_commands=["xcode-select"], check=False)
    if result.return_code != 0 or "not found" in result.stderr:
        fail("Xcode Command Line Tools are required. Run 'xcode-select --install' and try again.")

    # Accept Xcode license
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # After Xcode or CLT updates, the license often needs re-acceptance.
    # Failing to do so can cause build errors for ports.
    # (Source: https://trac.macports.org/wiki/ProblemHotlist)
    log.info("Attempting to accept Xcode license...")
    shell.exec(
        "sudo xcodebuild -license accept",
        allowed_commands=["xcodebuild"],
        check=False # Don't fail if already accepted or no Xcode installed
    )

def rollback():
    """No specific rollback actions for prepare phase."""
    pass
"
    },
    "install": {
      "filename": "install.star",
      "content": "# macports/install.star - Install phase for MacPorts

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# MacPorts .pkg installers are specific to the macOS version.
# Using a .pkg for a different macOS version can lead to installation failures
# or runtime issues. Always ensure the correct .pkg is downloaded.
# (Source: https://www.macports.org/install.php)

def install():
    """Install MacPorts."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _install_darwin()
    return {"install": True}

def _get_macos_version_info():
    """Helper to get macOS major version and codename for MacPorts PKG URL."""
    os_major_version = platform.version.split('.')[0] # e.g., "14" from "14.5.0"
    version_map = {
        "26": {"version_str": "26", "codename": "Tahoe"},
        "15": {"version_str": "15", "codename": "Sequoia"},
        "14": {"version_str": "14", "codename": "Sonoma"},
        "13": {"version_str": "13", "codename": "Ventura"},
    }
    return version_map.get(os_major_version, None)

def _install_darwin():
    """Install MacPorts on macOS via PKG installer."""
    version_info = _get_macos_version_info()
    if not version_info:
        fail(f"Unsupported macOS version: {platform.version}. MacPorts PKG installer not available for this version.")

    pkg_version_str = version_info["version_str"]
    pkg_codename = version_info["codename"]
    macports_base_version = "2.11.6" # From slots url_pattern

    pkg_url = f"https://github.com/macports/macports-base/releases/download/v{macports_base_version}/MacPorts-{macports_base_version}-{pkg_version_str}-{pkg_codename}.pkg"
    pkg_name = f"MacPorts-{macports_base_version}-{pkg_version_str}-{pkg_codename}.pkg"
    temp_path = f"/tmp/{pkg_name}"

    log.info(f"Downloading MacPorts PKG from: {pkg_url}")
    http.download(pkg_url, temp_path)

    log.info(f"Installing MacPorts PKG: {temp_path}")
    shell.exec(
        f"sudo installer -pkg {temp_path} -target /",
        allowed_commands=["installer"],
    )
    fs.remove(temp_path)

    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # After installation, MacPorts creates a dedicated 'macports' user and group
    # for security isolation. This is a core design principle.
    # (Source: https://guide.macports.org)
    # No action needed here, just documentation.

def rollback():
    """Remove MacPorts and all installed ports."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        log.info("Uninstalling all MacPorts ports...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo port -f uninstall installed",
            allowed_commands=["port"],
            check=False # Allow failure if no ports are installed
        )

        # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
        # On macOS 10.15 (Catalina) and later, the 'macports' user must be
        # deleted BEFORE removing the /opt/local directory, otherwise
        # the user deletion might fail due to files owned by 'macports' user.
        # (Source: MacPorts uninstall notes in slots)
        log.info("Removing macports user and group...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo dscl . -delete /Users/macports",
            allowed_commands=["dscl"],
            check=False # Allow failure if user doesn't exist
        )
        shell.exec(
            "sudo dscl . -delete /Groups/macports",
            allowed_commands=["dscl"],
            check=False # Allow failure if group doesn't exist
        )

        log.info("Removing MacPorts files and directories...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo rm -rf /opt/local /Applications/MacPorts /Library/LaunchAgents/org.macports.* /Library/LaunchDaemons/org.macports.*",
            allowed_commands=["rm"],
        )
"

    "provision": {
      "filename": "provision.star",
      "content": "# macports/provision.star - Provision phase for MacPorts

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# It is critical to run `sudo port -v selfupdate` immediately after installation
# and before installing any ports. This synchronizes MacPorts with the latest
# port definitions and ensures you're using up-to-date software.
# (Source: https://www.macports.org/install.php)

def provision():
    """Perform post-installation configuration for MacPorts."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _provision_darwin()
    return {"provision": True}

def _provision_darwin():
    """macOS specific provisioning for MacPorts."""
    log.info("Running MacPorts selfupdate...")
    shell.exec(
        "sudo port -v selfupdate",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )

    # Add MacPorts binaries to PATH for the current session
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # For MacPorts commands to be accessible without full path,
    # /opt/local/bin and /opt/local/sbin must be in the user's PATH.
    # This typically involves modifying shell configuration files (.bashrc, .zshrc).
    # This script only sets it for the current execution environment.
    # (Source: MacPorts install notes in slots)
    current_path = env.get("PATH", "")
    new_path = "/opt/local/bin:/opt/local/sbin"
    if new_path not in current_path:
        env.set("PATH", f"{new_path}:{current_path}")
        log.info(f"Added {new_path} to PATH for current session.")
    else:
        log.info(f"MacPorts paths already in PATH.")

def rollback():
    """No specific rollback for provision phase, as PATH changes are session-specific."""
    pass

    "verify": {
      "filename": "verify.star",
      "content": "# macports/verify.star - Verify phase for MacPorts

def verify():
    """Verify MacPorts installation and basic functionality."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        return _verify_darwin()
    return {"verify": False}

def _verify_darwin():
    """Verify MacPorts on macOS."""
    log.info("Verifying MacPorts version...")
    result = shell.exec(
        "port version",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
        log_output=True
    )
    if "Version:" not in result.stdout:
        log.error("MacPorts version check failed.")
        return {"verify": False}

    log.info("Performing functional test: listing installed ports...")
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # `port list installed` is a good functional test as it interacts with
    # the MacPorts registry and verifies basic command execution.
    # (Source: MacPorts verification notes in slots)
    result = shell.exec(
        "port list installed",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
        log_output=True,
        check=False # It's okay if no ports are installed yet
    )
    if result.return_code != 0 and "No ports are installed" not in result.stdout:
        log.error("MacPorts functional test (list installed ports) failed.")
        return {"verify": False}

    log.info("MacPorts installation verified successfully.")
    return {"verify": True}

def rollback():
    """No rollback actions for verification phase."""
    pass

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:

def prepare():

    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _prepare_darwin()

def _prepare_darwin():
    """Check macOS preconditions for MacPorts."""
    # Check for Xcode Command Line Tools
    result = shell.exec("xcode-select -p", allowed_commands=["xcode-select"], check=False)
    if result.return_code != 0 or "not found" in result.stderr:
        fail("Xcode Command Line Tools are required. Run 'xcode-select --install' and try again.")

    # Accept Xcode license

    log.info("Attempting to accept Xcode license...")
    shell.exec(
        "sudo xcodebuild -license accept",
        allowed_commands=["xcodebuild"],
        check=False # Don't fail if already accepted or no Xcode installed

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# MacPorts .pkg installers are specific to the macOS version.
# Using a .pkg for a different macOS version can lead to installation failures
# or runtime issues. Always ensure the correct .pkg is downloaded.
# (Source: https://www.macports.org/install.php)

def install():
    """Install MacPorts."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _install_darwin()
    return {"install": True}

def _get_macos_version_info():
    """Helper to get macOS major version and codename for MacPorts PKG URL."""
    os_major_version = platform.version.split('.')[0] # e.g., "14" from "14.5.0"
    version_map = {
        "26": {"version_str": "26", "codename": "Tahoe"},
        "15": {"version_str": "15", "codename": "Sequoia"},
        "14": {"version_str": "14", "codename": "Sonoma"},
        "13": {"version_str": "13", "codename": "Ventura"},
    }
    return version_map.get(os_major_version, None)

def _install_darwin():
    """Install MacPorts on macOS via PKG installer."""
    version_info = _get_macos_version_info()
    if not version_info:
        fail(f"Unsupported macOS version: {platform.version}. MacPorts PKG installer not available for this version.")

    pkg_version_str = version_info["version_str"]
    pkg_codename = version_info["codename"]
    macports_base_version = "2.11.6" # From slots url_pattern

    pkg_url = f"https://github.com/macports/macports-base/releases/download/v{macports_base_version}/MacPorts-{macports_base_version}-{pkg_version_str}-{pkg_codename}.pkg"
    pkg_name = f"MacPorts-{macports_base_version}-{pkg_version_str}-{pkg_codename}.pkg"
    temp_path = f"/tmp/{pkg_name}"

    log.info(f"Downloading MacPorts PKG from: {pkg_url}")
    http.download(pkg_url, temp_path)

    log.info(f"Installing MacPorts PKG: {temp_path}")
    shell.exec(
        f"sudo installer -pkg {temp_path} -target /",
        allowed_commands=["installer"],
    )
    fs.remove(temp_path)

    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # After installation, MacPorts creates a dedicated 'macports' user and group
    # for security isolation. This is a core design principle.
    # (Source: https://guide.macports.org)
    # No action needed here, just documentation.

def rollback():
    """Remove MacPorts and all installed ports."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        log.info("Uninstalling all MacPorts ports...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo port -f uninstall installed",
            allowed_commands=["port"],
            check=False # Allow failure if no ports are installed
        )

        # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
        # On macOS 10.15 (Catalina) and later, the 'macports' user must be
        # deleted BEFORE removing the /opt/local directory, otherwise
        # the user deletion might fail due to files owned by 'macports' user.
        # (Source: MacPorts uninstall notes in slots)
        log.info("Removing macports user and group...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo dscl . -delete /Users/macports",
            allowed_commands=["dscl"],
            check=False # Allow failure if user doesn't exist
        )
        shell.exec(
            "sudo dscl . -delete /Groups/macports",
            allowed_commands=["dscl"],
            check=False # Allow failure if group doesn't exist
        )

        log.info("Removing MacPorts files and directories...")
        shell.exec(
            "sudo rm -rf /opt/local /Applications/MacPorts /Library/LaunchAgents/org.macports.* /Library/LaunchDaemons/org.macports.*",
            allowed_commands=["rm"],
        )

# TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
# It is critical to run `sudo port -v selfupdate` immediately after installation

def provision():

    if platform.os == "darwin":
        _provision_darwin()
    return {"provision": True}

def _provision_darwin():
    """macOS specific provisioning for MacPorts."""
    log.info("Running MacPorts selfupdate...")
    shell.exec(
        "sudo port -v selfupdate",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
    )

    # Add MacPorts binaries to PATH for the current session
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # For MacPorts commands to be accessible without full path,
    # /opt/local/bin and /opt/local/sbin must be in the user's PATH.
    # This typically involves modifying shell configuration files (.bashrc, .zshrc).
    # This script only sets it for the current execution environment.
    # (Source: MacPorts install notes in slots)
    current_path = env.get("PATH", "")
    new_path = "/opt/local/bin:/opt/local/sbin"
    if new_path not in current_path:
        env.set("PATH", f"{new_path}:{current_path}")
        log.info(f"Added {new_path} to PATH for current session.")
    else:
        log.info(f"MacPorts paths already in PATH.")

def rollback():
    """No specific rollback for provision phase, as PATH changes are session-specific."""

def verify():
    """Verify MacPorts installation and basic functionality."""
    if platform.os == "darwin":
        return _verify_darwin()
    return {"verify": False}

def _verify_darwin():
    """Verify MacPorts on macOS."""
    log.info("Verifying MacPorts version...")
    result = shell.exec(
        "port version",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
        log_output=True
    )
    if "Version:" not in result.stdout:
        log.error("MacPorts version check failed.")
        return {"verify": False}

    log.info("Performing functional test: listing installed ports...")
    # TRIBAL KNOWLEDGE:
    # `port list installed` is a good functional test as it interacts with
    # the MacPorts registry and verifies basic command execution.
    # (Source: MacPorts verification notes in slots)
    result = shell.exec(
        "port list installed",
        allowed_commands=["port"],
        log_output=True,
        check=False # It's okay if no ports are installed yet
    )
    if result.return_code != 0 and "No ports are installed" not in result.stdout:
        log.error("MacPorts functional test (list installed ports) failed.")
        return {"verify": False}

    log.info("MacPorts installation verified successfully.")
    return {"verify": True}

def rollback():
    """No rollback actions for verification phase."""
